known.title: Not done: live CI waits do not block forge upgrade

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 3, Harm 3
Raise: Not done. Case: normal use - a close or land command is waiting for CI after its review and test lanes have emptied. `src/forge/checks.py:96` records that wait as a run with the live Forge process identity, but `src/forge/upgrade.py:93` checks only machine lane entries. Consequently, upgrade can replace the installed release while that command is still running; the command later resumes and can import code from the replacement release. `src/forge/land.py:410` also distinguishes live CI waits from lane entries. The new test covers reads, intake and reviews but misses this live run.

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Test. Case: normal use - an interrupted review's lane has already been cleared before upgrade, or an unrelated process has reused an ended run's PID. The review case invokes upgrade at line 73 and only checks for `lane left` afterward. The upgrade itself calls `machine.entries()`, whose cleanup writes that event in `src/forge/machine.py:763`; the test therefore does not establish the reported `end_known: false` history before the command. A refusal based on an already-present event could pass this test. The test also waits for the numeric PIDs to disappear at line 72, so it never checks the required start identity when a PID is reused; the existing reuse test at `tests/test_pid_reuse_keeps_run.py:98` exercises the board, not upgrade. Establish those states before invoking upgrade and check its installation decision.
findings.title: Gate: dead-process upgrade regression proof

why: forge upgrade refuses with 'Forge runs are still in progress' for runs whose process is gone: an intake read that joined its lane but never recorded an end, and a close review killed seconds after it started (lane left with end_known false); a client hit it on 20 Nov 2026 upgrading to v1.2.44 with no forge process running and had to install by hand
